purpose: Governance and report-generation schema for the ICHIBAN INSIGHT valuation workflow. This file tells the local program how to structure deterministic math handoff, guide Mini GPT / GPT narrative generation, and produce a deep-dive, agent-grade CMA / pricing strategy report.

core_philosophy.meaning: The app must calculate, store, and pass all deterministic facts, filters, metrics, adjustments, 1004MC rates, time adjustments, and pricing outputs before GPT writes narrative analysis.
core_philosophy.gpt_role: GPT should not invent the valuation. GPT should explain what the program did, what affected value, why it mattered, and how it affects the seller's going-to-market strategy.
core_philosophy.seller_question_to_answer: What is likely to happen to this specific property if it goes to market now, and what pricing or presentation choices could make the outcome faster, slower, stronger, or weaker?

layer_1_user_input: subject property PDF upload, preferably CoreLogic Realist when available
Zillow estimate, Redfin estimate, RealAVM or other AVM values when provided
agent notes, condition notes, showing readiness notes, and estimated days until market
layer_3_output: optional print/PDF output generated from the clean report, not Streamlit browser UI

do_not_print_or_export: private adjustment rule internals unless intentionally summarized

local_development.streamlit_note: The Streamlit page should preview the clean report and provide export buttons, but the exported report must not be created by printing the app screen.

runtime_mode.writing_goal: Produce an impressive, informative, and useful property-specific market summary that a Realtor would be excited to review, even if the conclusion is conservative.

online_estimates.use_policy: Online estimates are benchmarks only. They should be compared to the adjusted comparable evidence but should not override MLS-based valuation support.

hidden_backend_views.market_data_master: Full normalized MLS export with all statuses preserved.
hidden_backend_views.market_data_closed_for_pricing: Closed rows used for comp pricing, adjustment, and reconciliation.
hidden_backend_views.market_data_market_status: Active, Pending, Closed, Withdrawn, Expired, and other statuses used for market tone and momentum.
hidden_backend_views.market_data_gpt_review: Reduced safe payload for GPT narrative, including relevant metrics, remarks, and selected/rejected comp rationale.
hidden_backend_views.subject_profile_ready: Verified subject profile after PDF/manual intake reconciliation.
hidden_backend_views.analysis_payload: Final structured JSON package passed to GPT after math calculations are complete.

workflow_steps.program_action: Attempt subject PDF extraction first; use manual fallback when PDF extraction is incomplete.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain data limitations only when relevant; do not overemphasize technical intake issues in the client-facing report.

workflow_steps.program_action: Normalize column names, status values, dates, prices, concessions, square footage, basement, garage, remarks, and subdivision fields.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Do not discuss raw normalization unless data limitations materially affect confidence.

workflow_steps.program_action: Determine radius, subdivision, custom micro-market, property type, style, price band, and time period used.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain why the chosen market scope is appropriate and whether the analysis had to start wide before narrowing.

workflow_steps.program_action: Segment the data into Active, Pending, Closed, and other statuses and calculate baseline metrics.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Translate counts and price distributions into a practical market condition summary.

workflow_steps.program_action: Calculate absorption, months of inventory, and momentum using the ICHIBAN formula.

interpretation_guidance.compare_pending_vs_active_dim: Fast pending DIM with slow active DIM suggests buyers act quickly only when price/condition are aligned.
interpretation_guidance.compare_subject_to_momentum: Determine whether subject is likely to outperform, match, or underperform local market speed.

workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain what the local radius/micro-market suggests about seller timeline, buyer urgency, and pricing sensitivity.

workflow_steps.program_action: Calculate and store market change rates before time adjustments are applied.

classification_thresholds.note: Thresholds may be adjusted by configuration after testing against local MLS behavior.

workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain whether the market is increasing, stable, or declining and why older sales were or were not time-adjusted.

workflow_steps.program_action: Start broad when needed, narrow to the best competitive set, and reject false anchors.

subject_sqft_filter_policy.above_grade_sqft_preferred_range: 85% to 110% of subject above-grade finished area when sufficient comps exist

workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain why the selected comps were useful and why weaker or misleading comps did not control value.

workflow_steps.program_action: Classify subject and comps into renovation/condition tiers when remarks, photos, notes, or structured fields support it.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain how condition and renovation tier influence buyer response, pricing resistance, and likely showing performance.

workflow_steps.program_action: Apply structured adjustments for measurable differences and supported qualitative differences.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain the largest adjustment drivers and how they moved the comp evidence up or down.

workflow_steps.program_action: Apply time adjustments using the stored 1004MC monthly market change rate when supported.
workflow_steps.formula: time_adjustment_percent = monthly_market_change_percent * months_since_sale; time_adjustment_amount = adjusted_price_before_time * time_adjustment_percent; time_adjusted_comp_price = adjusted_price_before_time + time_adjustment_amount
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain whether time adjustments materially affected the reconciliation or were minimal.

workflow_steps.program_action: Reconcile the adjusted and time-adjusted comp range with AVM benchmarks, local momentum, active competition, and subject positioning.

range_policy.seller_decision_note: Seller may choose to list within, above, or below the range after professional agent discussion.

workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Explain why the final range is appropriate, what supports the low end, what supports the high end, and why the recommended list price is practical.

workflow_steps.program_action: Send structured analysis payload to GPT only after deterministic steps are complete.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Produce a deep, agent-grade, property-specific market and pricing strategy report.

workflow_steps.program_action: Generate .docx and optional markdown/PDF from the final report object, not the Streamlit app page.
workflow_steps.gpt_explanation_goal: Not applicable. This is an export/rendering step.

comp_inclusion_policy.purpose: Control when detailed comparable tables should appear in the client-facing report.
comp_inclusion_policy.client_facing_note: Detailed comparable home data is most useful for clients who are planning to come to market within the next 30 days, when the most recent sales and active competition are most relevant to near-term pricing decisions. For clients with a longer planning horizon, this report emphasizes market summary, pricing guidance, and competitive positioning, with a recommendation to refresh the comparable property set closer to the expected listing date.
comp_inclusion_policy.recommended_recheck_window: Refresh the comparable sales set and competing listings when the client is within 30 days of listing, or sooner if market conditions shift materially.

gpt_narrative_rules.tone: professional, objective, confident, clear, and seller-ready
gpt_narrative_rules.paragraph_style: short paragraphs with strong section structure
gpt_narrative_rules.allowed_depth: as much detail as necessary to be useful and impressive
avoid: generic statements such as 'the market is balanced' without subject-specific explanation
changing logic between reports without explanation
must_include_analysis_of: whether this property is likely to sell faster or slower than the local average
what could move the subject upward in buyer perception
what timeline the seller should reasonably expect
how active competition affects launch strategy
how pending speed affects buyer urgency
how closed DIM affects realistic expectations
how condition and presentation could change market response

subject_specific_market_performance.interpretation_standard: Use local radius/micro-market evidence first. General county/metro market statements are background only.

report_sections.title: Executive Summary
report_sections.purpose: Summarize the conclusion, suggested list range, recommended list posture, and the main reason behind the valuation.
content_requirements: top three value constraints or risks

report_sections.title: Subject Property Overview
report_sections.purpose: Describe the subject property and identify key valuation-relevant traits.
content_requirements: condition and renovation tier if available

report_sections.title: Local Market Snapshot
report_sections.purpose: Summarize current local market evidence from the MLS pull.
content_requirements: average Days in MLS by status

report_sections.title: Market Momentum & Absorption
report_sections.purpose: Explain how quickly the local market is absorbing inventory and what that means for seller timeline.
content_requirements: comparison of active DIM vs pending DIM vs closed DIM

report_sections.title: 1004MC / Time Trend Analysis
report_sections.purpose: Explain market direction and whether time adjustments were applied.
content_requirements: impact of time adjustments on valuation
limitations if sample size is thin

report_sections.title: Subject-Specific Market Performance
report_sections.purpose: Answer what is likely to happen to this specific property in this local market.
content_requirements: presentation/condition recommendations that could improve market response

report_sections.title: Comparable Selection Explanation
report_sections.purpose: Explain how comps were selected, ranked, and rejected.
content_requirements: why rejected comps or false anchors did not control value

report_sections.title: Adjustment Summary
report_sections.purpose: Summarize the value effects from physical, condition, qualitative, concession, and time adjustments.
content_requirements: garage / site / special feature impact if applicable
largest upward and downward adjustment drivers

report_sections.title: How the Value Was Determined
report_sections.purpose: Reconcile raw comps, adjusted comps, time-adjusted comps, online estimates, and market conditions into a supported range.
content_requirements: online estimate average as benchmark only

report_sections.title: Suggested List Price Range
report_sections.purpose: Provide the final list range and list strategy.
content_requirements: recommended list price or recommended posture
risk of pricing above supported range

report_sections.title: Pricing Strategy Options
content_requirements: when each option would or would not make sense

report_sections.title: Risk Factors & Buyer Resistance
report_sections.purpose: Identify likely buyer objections and pricing risk.

report_sections.title: Agent Advisory Notes
report_sections.purpose: Provide agent-facing guidance useful for listing conversation and seller counseling.
content_requirements: how to explain range to seller
what to inspect or verify before final pricing
what questions to ask during walkthrough
what improvements or presentation items may matter most
how to respond if seller wants to price above range

report_sections.title: Market Timing & Recheck Recommendation
report_sections.purpose: Explain why timing matters and when to refresh the analysis.
content_requirements: recommended 30-45 day recheck if not listing soon

report_sections.title: Disclaimer
report_sections.purpose: Clarify that the analysis is a professional estimate and decision-support tool, not a guarantee.
content_requirements: seller and Realtor final decision language
not guarantee of value or final sales price

text_blocks.market_estimate_disclaimer: This analysis is an estimate of potential market value based on currently available market data, comparable sales, and prevailing market conditions. It is intended to provide guidance and support pricing decisions, but it is not a guarantee of value or sales price. Real estate markets are dynamic and influenced by many factors beyond the control of the agent, seller, or analytical tools. Ultimately, market value is determined by buyer perception, buyer demand, and competing properties at the time the home is introduced to the open market. While this analysis incorporates objective data and current trends, buyer preferences, property presentation, financing conditions, and market competition may significantly influence the final outcome. Accordingly, this estimate should be considered a professional opinion based on available information and current market conditions. Actual market performance may vary.
text_blocks.methodology_disclaimer: The ICHIBAN analysis is designed to provide a structured, data-driven estimate of potential market value. The analysis incorporates objective market data sourced from the Multiple Listing Service (MLS), as reported by participating real estate agents, along with available public record information. While these sources are widely relied upon within the industry, both MLS and public record data may contain inaccuracies or incomplete information. The resulting summary is intended to serve as a professional decision-support tool. Final pricing decisions remain the responsibility of the licensed real estate professional and the property owner.
text_blocks.pricing_flexibility_statement: The Realtor and property owner may determine to list within the suggested range, above the range, or below the range based on professional judgment, client objectives, property presentation, and current market dynamics. Because the open market ultimately determines value, pricing strategy should remain flexible and responsive to buyer feedback and market activity once the property is listed.
factors_that_may_influence_final_market_: competing inventory at time of listing

quality_control_checks: Did the app calculate and store deterministic metrics before GPT narrative generation?
Did the report produce a suggested list price range?
Is the range tight enough unless data limitations justify a wider band?
Did the report explain whether time adjustments were applied?
Did the report include 1004MC annual and monthly market change when available?
Did the report distinguish local micro-market behavior from general market commentary?
Did the report explain likely subject-specific timeline compared to local average?
Did the report identify what could move the property up or slow it down?
Did the report discuss active competition and buyer resistance?
Did the report explain why comps were selected and why false anchors were rejected?
Did the report include both positive and limiting factors?
Did the report avoid unsupported certainty and overly promotional language?
Did the report include the required methodology/disclaimer section?
Did the report exclude Streamlit controls, debug outputs, private prompts, and raw engine dumps?
Did the exported .docx read like a professional agent-facing valuation report?

recommended_next_build_sequence: repair subject PDF extraction with manual fallback retained
preserve full MLS master file and create hidden views
build market metrics and momentum engine
rewrite GPT report prompt using this governance file
separate app preview from final report export
implementation_notes.important_warning: Do not let GPT perform hidden math that the program should calculate. GPT may interpret, explain, and advise, but the local engine should own repeatable calculations.

ruler_range.formatting_rule: Labels and dollar amounts must not overlap in the Word/docx output.
ruler_range.purpose: Show the practical pricing lane, not a guaranteed result.

days_in_mls_policy.seller_facing_metric: Average DIM / Average Days in MLS
days_in_mls_policy.reason: Average DIM reflects real exposure time and matches how sellers think about likely market time.

market_momentum_policy.definition: Momentum equals speed/activity of the market, not price.
market_momentum_policy.labeling_rule: Avoid confusing multiple MOI-style labels. If a momentum pressure metric is used, explain it clearly as a practical current-supply indicator, not standard appraisal MOI.

seller_facing_categories: Above-Grade Living Area / Main Floor Space
seller_repeatable_lines: Not all square footage is valued the same.
Basements add value, but not the same as main-floor space.
Buyers pay more for what feels finished.
How the home lives matters as much as size.
Price per square foot is a helpful reference, but buyers do not buy homes that way; they compare the whole property.
adjustment_story_policy.main_report_rule: Do not show a long line-by-line adjustment spreadsheet in the seller-facing report unless specifically requested.

micro_market_signal_policy.purpose: Help the Realtor explain why the selected market set is relevant and how live competition affects positioning.

seller_facing_language_restrictions.rule: The report should sound like the Realtor is presenting organized market evidence, not defending a price or exposing backend tools.

disclaimer_policy.paragraph_rule: Keep the full disclaimer paragraph; only simplify the heading from Methodology & Disclaimer to Disclaimer.
